text:
I


I return to you, solitude, empty water,

water of my images, so dead,

cloud of my words, so deserted,

night of unsayable poetry.


Through you the same blood—yours and mine—

runs to the soul of no one, forever open.

Through you anguish is the shadow of the door

that opens neither by night nor by day.


I follow childhood in your prison, and the game

that alternates deaths and resurrections

from one image to another lives blind.


The wind, the sun, and the sea of travel cry out.

I devour my own hearts

and play with the eyes of the landscape.


II


Which of all the shadows is mine?

Beauty comes to every body

and anticipates in the air the feat

of being poetry without the poem.

June entrusts two magic clouds to me

and I am already the sky where doubt begins.

Will I so soon rest my head

on the deep hand that is not yet mine?


In words of love the beautiful

life goes by with thorn and rose,

always so high that when we find her

the fingers first bleed on the thorn;

and the rose high in its branches

is already another rose, becoming indeterminate.


III


June gave me the voice, the silent

music of keeping a feeling silent.

Now June carries away, like the wind,

the sweetest, most spacious hope.


From my voice I drew the clean rose,

the moment’s only eternal rose.

Love did not take it; the wind took it,

and the soul was uselessly joyful.


After a year of dying every day,

the fruits of my voice said so much

and so silently that for some days


they lived in the shadow of that song.

(Here the voice breaks, and the terror

of so much solitude fills the days.)

translation.title: Hours of June
translation.editorial_note: The three numbered sonnets are preserved, including their formal repetitions of June, solitude, rose, voice, and silence. The clear OCR glyph ‘A1’ is read as ‘Al.’
